title: Peach Picnic Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft peach cupcakes with light peach frosting, ready in about 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake.
description: These cupcakes taste like a summer picnic in a paper wrapper. I fold real diced peaches into the batter, so every bite has soft fruit and a light crumb. The frosting uses peach puree instead of extra liquid, so it stays thick enough to swirl tall. I tested this batch on a hot July afternoon and the peaches held their shape through baking. A fresh peach slice on top makes it look like it just came off the porch table.
ingredients: 1 cup fresh peaches, peeled and finely diced
1/4 cup peach puree (from ripe fresh peach)
1 fresh peach, thinly sliced, for garnish
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a muffin tin with 12 paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a medium bowl.
Beat 1/2 cup butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla.
Alternate adding the flour mix and buttermilk, mixing just until combined.
Fold in diced peaches gently with a spatula.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two-thirds full.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cupcakes in the tin for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool fully.
Beat 1 cup butter until smooth, then add powdered sugar in two batches.
Mix in peach puree until the frosting is smooth and holds soft peaks.
Pipe frosting in a tall swirl on each cooled cupcake and top with a peach slice.
tips: Pat diced peaches dry with a paper towel before folding in, so the batter does not turn watery.
Chill the peach puree for 10 minutes before mixing it into frosting, so the buttercream stays thick enough to pipe.
If peaches are out of season, thawed and well drained frozen peaches work fine.
Add peach garnish slices right before serving so they do not brown or weep onto the frosting.

faq.question: Can I use canned peaches instead of fresh?
faq.answer: Yes, but drain them well and pat dry with paper towels first. Canned peaches hold more liquid, which can make the batter dense.

faq.question: Why did my peach frosting turn soupy?
faq.answer: Peach puree adds extra moisture, so add it slowly and stop once the frosting holds a soft peak. Chilling the puree first also helps.

faq.question: How do I keep the peach garnish from browning?
faq.answer: Toss sliced peaches in a little lemon juice and add them just before serving, not before storing the cupcakes.

faq.question: Can I make these cupcakes ahead of time?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to two days ahead and store unfrosted at room temperature in an airtight container. Frost and garnish the same day you plan to serve them.

conclusion: These peach cupcakes bring picnic season straight to your kitchen table. Bake them the day of your gathering for the freshest peach flavor and prettiest garnish.
